A 32-year-old female patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus and coronary heart disease presents for her
annual checkup. She is currently on metformin, enalapril, and aspirin. Recent blood bank screening
from two weeks ago shows a nonreactive HIV-1/2 combination immunoassay. Upon reviewing her
chart, the physician discovers a reactive HIV-1/2 combination immunoassay from last year's visit,
ordered by another physician in the practice. The patient appears unaware of this previous result. After
informing the patient about the previous HIV test result, what is the most appropriate next step for the
physician? Answer Choices: (A) Apologize to the patient for the delay in informing her about the initial
test results (B) Recommend that the patient undergo HIV confirmatory testing at the blood bank (C)
Refer the patient to an infectious disease specialist for further evaluation (D) Request the patient's
permission to perform an HIV nucleic acid amplification test (E) Perform a CD4 count to assess
immune status before further testing (F) Speak to the colleague who ordered the initial HIV test (G)

Inform the patient that the discrepancy in results may indicate a false-positive result last year (H)
Advise the patient to continue routine follow-up without further testing (I) Disclose to the patient that a
colleague forgot to follow up on the results of the initial HIV test (J) Repeat the HIV-1/2 combination
immunoassay immediately
 A. Advise the patient to continue routine follow-up without further testing
B. Disclose to the patient that a colleague forgot to follow up on the results of the initial HIV test
C. Repeat the HIV-1/2 combination immunoassay immediately
D. Perform a CD4 count to assess immune status before further testing
E. Request the patient's permission to perform an HIV nucleic acid amplification test
F. Refer the patient to an infectious disease specialist for further evaluation
G. Recommend that the patient undergo HIV confirmatory testing at the blood bank
H. Inform the patient that the discrepancy in results may indicate a false-positive result last year
I. Speak to the colleague who ordered the initial HIV test
J. Apologize to the patient for the delay in informing her about the initial test results
